description: This horizontal bar chart illustrates the difference in average Word Error Rate (WER) between two models—NESAC ft model (orange bars) and SESHA ft model (green bars)—when various optimisations are applied, with the y-axis listing the optimisations applied in descending order of their impact: “Normalised”, “Add Spacing”, “Remove Spacing”, “Americanisms”, and “Dates”. The x-axis represents the “Difference in Average WER from Whisper large”, scaled linearly from 0.000 to approximately 0.0035, with tick marks at intervals of 0.001. For each optimisation, two bars are shown side-by-side, with the orange bar representing the NESAC ft model and the green bar representing the SESHA ft model. The values are explicitly labeled at the end of each bar: for “Normalised”, the NESAC ft model shows a difference of 0.00334 and the SESHA ft model 0.00323; for “Add Spacing”, 0.00319 and 0.00344 respectively; for “Remove Spacing”, 0.00311 and 0.00306; for “Americanisms”, 0.00299 and 0.00302; and for “Dates”, 0.00257 and 0.00228. The bars are not sorted by value but are presented in a fixed order from top to bottom, and there is no visual emphasis such as shading or bolding on any specific bar. A legend at the bottom confirms the color coding for each model.
